channel.title: SUBSUELO FS — Production guides
channel.description: Direct guides for music prompts, negative prompts and sound direction.

item.title: What is a negative prompt in music and when should you use one?
item.description: What it removes, where it goes and when it helps with vocals, instruments or finish.

item.title: How to write music prompts that give a clear direction
item.description: A practical structure for genre, pulse, drums, low end, source material, space and mix.

item.title: How to describe drums in a music prompt and avoid the default groove
item.description: Concrete vocabulary for describing drums in a music prompt: pocket, source families, swing, density and the mistakes that flatten a groove.

item.title: 808, sub-bass and movement: controlling the low end in a music prompt
item.description: Which words select a sub, an 808 or a bassline in a music prompt, how to describe movement, and how to clean a muddy low end with negative prompts.

item.title: Why AI music sounds generic and the prompt habits that fix it
item.description: Generic AI music comes from vague prompts averaged into the genre's middle. Source words, space, exclusions and one-axis iteration fix it.

item.title: Space, texture and dirt: writing the room into your prompt
item.description: Reverb space, echo, tape and degradation vocabulary for music prompts: dry vs washed, dub delay, vinyl crackle, and how much dirt is too much.

item.title: How to make dark trap: a prompt built on dry drums, a lead 808 and ritual texture
item.description: How to make dark trap with prompts: dry programmed drums, a dominant 808 that carries the melody, ritual texture, and the exclusions that keep EDM out.

item.title: How to make dark UK garage: 2-step pocket, short subs, narrow space
item.description: How to make dark UK garage with prompts: shuffled 2-step drums, displaced snares, short sub hits, minimal stabs and the exclusions that keep house out.

item.title: How to make dark jungle: chopped breaks over a slow, heavy sub
item.description: How to make dark jungle with a prompt: chopped breaks as the lead, slow heavy sub, tape and vinyl degradation, dub echo and what to exclude.

item.title: How to make noir hip-hop: dark boom bap, prompt by prompt
item.description: How to make noir hip-hop with prompts: dusty jazz sources, swung boom bap drums, upright bass, smoky rooms, tape finish, and the exclusions that keep it dark.

item.title: How to make abstract hip-hop: dark experimental beats, prompt by prompt
item.description: How to make abstract hip-hop with prompts: degraded sources, drunk drum pockets, static sub pressure, space as an instrument, and what to exclude.

item.title: How to make dark dub hip-hop: dry drums and the delay as the lead instrument
item.description: How to make dub hip-hop with prompts: dark rap-weight drums, a sustained sub, dub delay as the lead instrument, and the exclusions that keep ska out.
